title: Coinbase customer-support insider data theft
confirmed_facts: Coinbase reported that criminals bribed or recruited a small group of overseas support agents to copy customer data from support tools.
Coinbase reported exposure of identity, contact, masked financial, government-ID image, balance snapshot, transaction-history, and limited corporate data for a subset of customers.
Coinbase reported that login credentials, 2FA codes, private keys, and direct ability to move funds were not obtained through this access.
Coinbase added extra checks for large withdrawals on flagged accounts and described stronger support-operation controls and monitoring.
inferences: Support access must be modeled as a product security plane even when it cannot directly move money, because exposed context can enable downstream social engineering.
failure_patterns: support data used for targeted social engineering
high-impact withdrawal risk following data theft
trust_boundaries: support tool to document and transaction data
exposed customer context to high-impact withdrawal flow
control_hypotheses: Support role design should minimize visible fields and distinguish masked display from authorized reveal.
Bulk and anomalous access controls should operate per agent, case, customer, field class, and time window.
Known data-exposure signals should raise transaction assurance without relying on the same support channel.

regression.mutation: Add unrestricted customer export or impersonation with no case reason, expiry, field projection, or anomaly event; compose separately with a high-impact withdrawal fixture.
